assessment.text: The premise is true: the 8-K reports that Huang resigned as President, CEO and director with immediate effect, so 'Jensen is gone' is a fact of the record, not a forecast.

The thesis is the step from his departure to a reason to buy, and nothing in the record backs it: the filing does not say the exit helps shareholders, and what replaces him is an interim CEO who also stays CFO while the Board searches.

His exit removes no visible drag: in the last quarter he ran, revenue growth sped up by 20.6 percentage points and operating margin rose 5.4 percentage points on a year earlier, so the record points the other way from a 'better without him' story.
The two corollaries hold, but both measure the quarter ended 2026-07-26, before the resignation, so they describe his tenure and cannot show any effect of his leaving.
The turnover goes beyond the CEO: the head of Worldwide Field Operations and the Chief Accounting Officer are both retiring, which deepens the transition risk the new team carries.

The valuation, at a 2026-09-30 price set before the resignation, needs 13.4% a year for 10 years with operating margin held at 65.2%, a pace 0 of 40 filers that started at its size reached; a leadership change matters to that price mainly if it threatens the margin assumption, which the record gives no reason to expect will improve.

case_for.text: The factual premise is confirmed by the newest filing, and the operating results the new team inherits were still improving, with the newest quarter's operating margin the highest of the last eight.

The growth the 2026-09-30 price needs sits well below the company's own +100.0% a year over its last three fiscal years, so the price does not demand that new leadership repeat the past pace; this is a case about the business, though, not about Huang's exit.

case_against.text: An interim CEO holding the CFO job at the same time, during an open search, is a source of uncertainty, not a new strategy, and the record names no change in direction that his departure would unlock.

The price leans most on the 65.2% margin held for ten years: at the industry's 90th-percentile margin of 26.6% the same price would need 28.1% a year, so any erosion during the transition would cut against the buy case rather than for it.
The successor inherits working capital that is already stretching, with receivable days at 59.6 against 54.1 and inventory days at 119.3 against 105.6 a year before.

The first quarters under interim and then permanent leadership will show whether the margin the price depends on holds; who the Board names as permanent CEO is the other open fact.

assessment.text: As worded the premise is false: fiscal 2026 revenue rose 65.5%, and the doubling line was missed by $45.06B, so the claim is wrong on the basis it names.

The claim appears to describe something real under the wrong label. Only the newest quarter, Q2 FY2027, grew 105.9% on a year earlier. That makes doubling a current-quarter fact, not a fiscal-2026 one.
The fiscal-year path tells the opposite story: FY2026 was the year growth slowed, by 48.7 percentage points after +114.2% in FY2025.
Gross profit and operating income also failed to double in fiscal 2026, so the shortfall is not an artifact of the revenue line alone.

For the buy decision, what matters is what the price asks. At the 2026-09-30 price, the implied growth is 13.4% a year for 10 years, well under recent growth whether or not the doubling is true. That figure leans most on holding a 65.2% operating margin; at the industry 90th percentile margin of 26.6% the same price needs 28.1%.
The record cannot say whether the quarterly reacceleration lasts. Of 40 ten-year spans of filers at this size, 0 grew even at the implied rate, so past growth is weak support for any forecast.

case_for.text: Read charitably as a statement about current momentum, the claim holds: the latest quarter grew 105.9%.
Deferred revenue rose 215.1% against revenue growth of 105.9%, so billings ahead of delivery outpaced recognized revenue.
Even the 65.5% that falsifies the claim ranked 6 of 63 in its industry, against a class median of 13.0%.

case_against.text: Doubling at this scale has no precedent among other large filers: it held in 0 of 366 company-years among filers with revenue of at least $100.00B.
Even among SIC 3674 filers with revenue of at least $100.0M it was rare and seldom lasted: it held in 15 of 1045 company-years, and only 3 of 12 still held a year later.

Receivables grew 126.8% against revenue growth of 105.9%, and receivable days rose to 59.6 from 54.1. The receivables corollary also held, by +1.3 points, which counts against the claim, so part of the growth is not yet collected cash.

Whether the price depends on doubling at all: it needs 13.4% a year at a 65.2% margin, so the decision turns more on margin durability than on this growth claim.

brief.summary: Thesis check on buying NVDA now: one claim supported, three challenged, one mixed. Huang's departure is confirmed (8-K, Nov 11, 2026), but it leaves an open succession, with CFO Kress as interim CEO. Performance was strong under him (Q2 FY27 revenue $96.22B, +105.9%), so the 'buy because he's gone' premise is challenged. Gross margin was supported at about 75% in each quarter shown. Fiscal 2026 revenue rose 65.5%, not doubling. Free cash flow ($96.68B) was below net income ($120.07B). Total revenue growth accelerated for three quarters, but China foreclosure and export-control design-outs challenge the data center thesis. Net: the core rationale fails, and fundamentals, not the CEO exit, should drive the decision.

analytics.label: Revenue growth the price implies (reverse DCF)
analytics.question: What growth does the price already assume?
analytics.formula: PV(g) = enterprise value $5.48T, solved for g between −50% and +100%
analytics.reading: At these assumptions the enterprise value of $5.48T needs revenue to grow 13.4% a year for 10 years, from $302.97B to $1.07T. The company's own revenue grew +100.0% a year over its last three fiscal years. The largest revenue any filer reported for 2025 is $716.92B (AMAZON.COM, INC.): the implied year-10 revenue is 1.5 times that. Of 40 ten-year spans of filers that started at its size (revenue of $151.48B to $605.94B; starts 2009 to 2015), 0 grew at least that fast (median 1.3% a year, 90th percentile 8.0%; 4 more could not be followed for ten years). With the operating margin at the industry's median of 4.2% (n = 61, 2025) instead of 65.2%, no growth from −50% to +100% a year reaches the price. With the operating margin at the industry's 90th percentile of 26.6% (n = 61, 2025) instead of 65.2%, the same price needs 28.1% a year. Across the grid (discount rate ±2 points, margin ±5 points) the implied growth runs from 6.5% to 19.7% a year (15 of 15 cells solve).
analytics.note: Arithmetic under stated assumptions, not a forecast and not advice: it says what constant growth the price would need if every assumption below held. Starting revenue $302.97B (Revenue, four quarters ended 2026-07-26). Operating margin 65.2%, every year: the trailing operating margin, $197.58B ÷ $302.97B. Tax on operating profit 21% (the US federal rate, a stated default). Sales-to-capital 1.47: trailing revenue $302.97B ÷ invested capital $205.76B (equity $228.98B + debt $33.37B − cash and securities $56.59B, 2026-07-26); each dollar of new revenue is assumed to need capital at this ratio. Discount rate 9% a year (a stated default, near a long-run US equity return). After 10 years, growth of 3% a year forever. Cash flow = revenue × margin × (1 − tax) − (revenue − last year's revenue) ÷ sales-to-capital; discounted at the end of each year; compared with the enterprise value. An implied growth is arithmetic: the growth at which a discounted cash flow under the stated assumptions equals the price. Change an assumption and it changes; it is not a forecast and not a price target. analysis.corollary_rule: A corollary is an implication a model proposed and code computed. Each is read by the grammar and by the typed form the proposing model wrote: two readers, which is weaker than the two-of-three rule the thesis's own claims are read under. A corollary never moves a verdict; when most of a claim's computed corollaries come out against it, the claim is flagged.
analysis.audit_rule: A sentence is verified by code when every id it cites is in this run, at least one is evidence, and every number it writes is carried by that evidence: a verified finding's quotes and cited figures, an analytic's value, inputs and reading, a computed test's operands and result, a reported figure, an 8-K event's text. The claim's own words carry no number, and neither does the sentence a model wrote for a corollary: only what code computed for it does. A threshold is a third thing: when a number equals the threshold of a computed test or corollary the sentence cites, or a condition's own threshold, the sentence is not failed for it, and it is listed as a threshold restated, not checked as a fact. A bare year is carried by a cited item dated in that year. The audit does not decide whether a sentence follows from what it cites.
analysis.persistence_method: Resampling with replacement: 10,000 paths of 4 quarters, each step drawn from the measure's own last N quarterly changes (differences in points for a percent, growth rates for an amount), from the current value; the share of paths in which the test holds in every one of the 4 quarters. Seed 20261118. It assumes the past changes are exchangeable: it ignores trend, seasonality and anything not in the facts. It describes the history; it is not a forecast.

weakest_why.text: The premise is true, but the step from it to buying is a claim about cause that the filings cannot test. The resignation filing says nothing about whether the departure benefits shareholders.
In the last quarter Huang ran, revenue growth sped up by 20.6 percentage points and operating margin rose 5.4 percentage points on a year earlier. The record shows no drag that his exit removes.
The turnover reaches beyond the CEO: the head of Worldwide Field Operations and the Chief Accounting Officer are both retiring. This adds transition risk rather than a defined new strategy.

strongest_for.text: The margin base is real and rare in its industry. Gross margin clears 70% in each of the last four quarters with 1.69x a typical move of room, and it ranks 4 of 63 among SIC 3674 filers.
Demand, read through total revenue, has not stalled. Growth reached 105.9% on a year earlier, revenue rose in each of the last 8 quarters, and deferred revenue grew +215.1%, faster than revenue.
The 13.4% a year the price needs sits far below the company's own +100.0% a year over its last three fiscal years. This holds only if the margin assumption holds too.

strongest_against.text: Earnings are converting to cash poorly. Operating cash flow was 0.70x net income over four quarters and 0.40x in Q2 FY2027, and cash conversion ranks 32 of 38 in the industry.
The price is fragile to the margin. At the industry's 90th-percentile operating margin of 26.6%, the same price needs 28.1% a year, and even the base 13.4% was matched by 0 of 40 comparable spans.

The high-margin streak is not the five-year norm. The test held in only 6 of 20 readings, part of the year-on-year gain is the earlier H20 charge dropping out, and inventory days rose to 119.3 days from 105.6 days.

bottom_line.text: The thesis's central claim is unsupported. Huang's resignation is a filed fact, but nothing in the record turns his departure into a reason to buy, and what replaces him is an interim CEO who also remains CFO while the Board searches.

The supporting claims split. Gross margin above 70% holds and revenue growth is speeding up on a year earlier, but fiscal 2026 revenue did not double and free cash flow fell short of net income, so two of the thesis's financial pillars fail as worded.

bottom_line.text: Every quarter in the record ends before the resignation, and the valuation is struck at a 2026-09-30 price, also before the 8-K. The record therefore cannot show how results or the price respond to the leadership change.

At that price the reverse DCF needs 13.4% a year for 10 years, a pace 0 of 40 filers at its size reached, and it leans most on a 65.2% operating margin held every year. That makes margin durability, not the CEO change or the doubling claim, the hinge of the decision.

Read on earnings the stock costs 28.5x, but its free cash flow yield is 2.3%, because receivables and inventory are absorbing cash that net income counts. The cash view is the less flattering basis for the decision.
